extracted.intended_audience: general readers, film viewers, researchers looking for information about the film
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia article summarizing the 1985 satirical road comedy film Lost in America (plot, cast, production, reception, and home media). Intended to inform readers about the film's content, release, critical reception, and legacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rotten Tomatoes rating and consensus
rubrics_metrics.description: Lost In America received mostly positive reviews from critics and holds a 95% rating on Rotten Tomatoes, based on 39 reviews. The site's consensus states: "A satire of the American fantasy of leaving it all behind, Lost in America features some of Albert Brooks' best, most consistent writing and cultural jabs."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses aggregate critic approval (percentage) and the site-written consensus as measures of critical reception; includes the number of reviews contributing to the rating (39).

rubrics_metrics.name: Metacritic weighted average score
rubrics_metrics.description: Metacritic, which uses a weighted average, assigned the film a score of 78 out of 100, based on 10 critics, indicating "generally favorable" reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a weighted-average numerical score and qualitative interpretation ('generally favorable'); notes the sample size (10 critics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Box office and budget (commercial success)
rubrics_metrics.description: Budget: $4 million; Box office: $10,179,000. The film was a commercial success, though not a blockbuster.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial performance (budget vs. gross) is presented as an indicator of commercial success; explicit phrasing qualifies scale of success ('not a blockbuster').

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry awards (Best Screenplay)
rubrics_metrics.description: The film's script won the National Society of Film Critics award for Best Screenplay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Winning recognized industry awards is cited as a measure of artistic/critical achievement for the screenplay specifically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notable critic endorsement (Roger Ebert)
rubrics_metrics.description: Roger Ebert gave it 4 out of 4 stars, calling it observant and very funny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prominent individual critic reviews and star ratings are presented as evidence of critical praise and perceived comedic quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion in 'funniest movies' rankings
rubrics_metrics.description: The film is #80 on Bravo's 100 Funniest Movies, and was listed at #84 on American Film Institute's AFI's 100 Years...100 Laughs in 2000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Placement on curated 'best/funniest' lists from recognized organizations/networks is used as a legacy/prestige metric indicating the film's standing in comedy history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion Collection selection (curatorial recognition)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Criterion Collection selected Lost in America as their first Albert Brooks film in the collection, releasing the Blu-ray on July 25, 2017.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection by a respected archival/curatorial label (Criterion) is presented as a mark of lasting critical and cultural value; associated home-media release dates are noted.
